items.event_time_ist: Night of Oct 12 into Oct 13, 2026 (expected formation window, local Pacific)
items.source_name: NHC (Tropical Weather Outlook, 5 PM PDT Oct 12)
items.summary: NHC's 5 PM PDT Oct 12 Tropical Weather Outlook raises EP93 - a broad low pressure several hundred miles south-southwest of Guatemala's coast - to near 100% formation chance through both 48 hours and 7 days. Showers and thunderstorms are beginning to show signs of organization; a tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to form well south of southern Mexico later tonight or tomorrow, moving west-northwest at ~10 mph.
items.title: EP93 at near-100% formation chance - NHC expects tropical depression or storm tonight or tomorrow

items.event_time_ist: Night of Saturday, Oct 10 (dive) / Sunday morning, Oct 11, 2026 (body recovered) - Mazatlan local time
items.summary: Juan 'Patines' (aka Juanito/El Chicali), a well-known cliff diver at Mazatlan's Glorieta Rodolfo Sanchez Taboada ('El Clavadista'), died Saturday night, Oct 10, after jumping into Simon-driven surf with waves up to 3 meters and being unable to reach the rocks. A fellow diver tried to save him but the swell defeated the rescue; municipal aquatic rescue teams resumed the search at 5 a.m. Sunday, Oct 11, and found his body near the same spot. Official identity still uncertain across outlets (some say Juan 'N' ~50, others Ricardo 'N' 35).
items.title: Mazatlan cliff diver 'Juan Patines' killed by Simon surf; body recovered Sunday

items.event_time_ist: Forecast for around midnight Thursday, Oct 15, 2026 (Mazatlan local time)
items.summary: Mexico's SMN coordinator Fabian Vazquez, speaking at the presidential press conference, said the forecast takes Simon northward while gradually weakening, with effects beginning around Wednesday and the closest approach/impact expected very near Mazatlan, Sinaloa, around midnight Thursday, Oct 15 - still a forecast, not confirmed. Consistent with NHC's Wed-Thu approach to Mexico's west-central coast.
items.title: Mexico's SMN: Simon expected near Mazatlan around midnight Thursday, Oct 15
